solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nice, open arrangement for seed-producer

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so the letters of these two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone praises a pleasantly open layout for a plant that produces seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' reorders the letters of NICE OPEN; 'for' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The woody cone of a conifer holds and releases the tree's seeds.

clue.text: A hairstyle for every month

parts.note: per means for each or for every, as in 'per day'

explanation.surface: A monthly visit to the salon for a new hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for permanent wave, it is a chemical treatment that sets curls in the hair.

clue.text: On the way up, left a vehicle connected to ships

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A climbing driver leaves a car linked to a fleet of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way up' reverses L, A and VAN in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to a navy or to warships and seafaring.

clue.text: Cheese feast in English tourist attraction

parts.note: Cheddar is a hard English cheese
to gorge is to feast greedily

explanation.surface: A cheese banquet held at a famous English sightseeing spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This limestone ravine in the Mendip Hills of Somerset is a popular English visitor site.

clue.text: Fantasy world of eccentric in Aran

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An oddball on the Aran Islands lives in a world of make-believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the definition to the wordplay; Aran is a group of islands off Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: C. S. Lewis created this imaginary land of talking animals, reached through a wardrobe.

clue.text: That is, I hesitate to say, dross

parts.note: sc. abbreviates the Latin scilicet, meaning 'that is to say' or 'namely'
um is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: A speaker reluctantly calls something rubbish, pausing before the insult.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet, Latin for 'namely') is an abbreviation seen in footnotes and dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words for worthless refuse, the impure froth skimmed off the top of molten metal or liquid.

clue.text: Stage where Queen, maybe, go missing?

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, signalled as an example by 'maybe'
an object that walks has disappeared, as if stolen

explanation.surface: A theatre where the monarch might fail to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests a monarch or the abbreviation ER, but here it is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised runway on which fashion models parade is a narrow platform, a kind of stage.

clue.text: Finished off rearing of French racehorse

indicators.note: a rearing horse rises up, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
Red Rum was the famous racehorse that won the Grand National three times

explanation.surface: A French racehorse rearing up finished off its rider's chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' reverses DE plus REDRUM; Red Rum, the celebrated British steeplechaser, conveniently spells its own reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish someone off is a colloquial way of saying to kill them.

clue.text: It's most unlike bacon could go up!

definitions.text: It's most unlike bacon could go up!

parts.words: It's most unlike bacon could go up!
parts.note: bacon comes from swine, and the saying about them taking to the air expresses something most improbable

explanation.surface: A wry remark that bacon is hardly likely to rise into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlike' is used in the old sense 'unlikely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a sarcastic retort to a statement meaning something will never happen.

clue.text: Show vicar up — embarrassing initially

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A command to expose a clergyman, the opening part being awkward for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a reversal signal for the vicar, but it is just a word whose first letter is taken, with that of 'embarrassing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs is a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Celebrate noisily one being included in catalogue

indicators.note: being included in places the one inside the catalogue's word

parts.note: a roster is a list of names, a catalogue of people on duty
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A party where one person is added to the guest list.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel boisterously and rowdily is an old-fashioned verb meaning make merry loudly.

clue.text: Some criminal — add in scavengers — finding place with valuables

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A criminal joins the scavengers in rummaging and stumbles on a hoard of treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale the hero finds a cave full of riches, so the phrase now means any place crammed with treasures.

clue.text: American season, note, to fizzle out

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
a flat is a musical note lowered by a semitone

explanation.surface: An autumn in the US whose musical note fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a joke or plan that fails to have its intended effect.

clue.text: Sources of wood and metal on the coast?

parts.note: the ash is a tree, a source of timber
ore is rock from which metal is extracted, so 'sources of' also applies here

explanation.surface: A question about where timber and metal come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sources of' serves both nouns: a tree for wood, a mineral for metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land beside the sea after leaving a boat is being on dry land at the coast.

clue.text: Best policy, perhaps, dispatching the nosy

indicators.note: dispatching sends things off in all directions, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: The best approach may be getting rid of busybodies.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the proverb that it is 'the best policy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says truthfulness is the best policy, so the virtue is described by that saying.

clue.text: Cream the French used as accompaniment to cheese?

parts.note: the cream of something is its best part, the pick
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Using a French cream as a side for cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangy chutney-like relish such as Branston is commonly served with cheese in Britain.

clue.text: Poorly in Paris one spring

parts.note: un is French for one, the Parisian word
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill in Paris one spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' reads as the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poorly is a British informal way of being ill or sick.

clue.text: US president's take on English county

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth US president; with the possessive his name gains an S
to hire something is to take it on for payment

explanation.surface: An American leader's view of an English region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take on' looks like 'opinion of', but 'take' means hire and 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large county in eastern England, the shire whose county town is Lincoln.

clue.text: Adherent of religion: one elevating a foreign emperor

indicators.note: elevating raises things up, so in this down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a tsar was the emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A believer in a faith that exalts a foreign emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevating' reverses A TSAR; the surface fits too, as the faith reveres Emperor Haile Selassie.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian is a follower of the Jamaican faith; the shortened form names a believer.

clue.text: Hero doing nothing to speak of

indicators.note: to speak of says the word for doing nothing is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: idle means doing nothing, inactive

explanation.surface: A hero who does next to nothing worth mentioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to speak of' looks like 'worth mentioning' but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone greatly admired and looked up to, a celebrity or role model, is a hero.

clue.text: Italian dish to drop, getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in puts the drooping word inside the road word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way
to sag is to droop or drop down

explanation.surface: Someone drops a pasta bake and it gets underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a baked Italian pasta dish of layered flat sheets with meat sauce and cheese.

clue.text: Married female exploited

parts.note: to be exploited is to be used

explanation.surface: A wife complains she has been taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined or united into one have been wedded together, a figurative sense of marrying.

clue.text: Teddy bears, say, coming in twos? Yes, regularly

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A question whether teddy bears come in pairs, answered with a yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy bears are an example of playthings for children, signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Cooperate in drama and dance

parts.note: a play is a drama on stage
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Taking part together in a theatrical production and a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means go along with someone, work together, as players passing the ball.
